title: Juhayna
description: Juhayna is Egypt's quintessential household food and beverage giant, celebrated since 1983 for continuously nourishing families across the nation through wholesome dairy products, fresh farm milks, rich yogurts, and natural juices. For over four decades, its vibrant four-petal flower emblem and heartfelt promise, Caring Everyday, have occupied a permanent place inside millions of breakfast tables and refrigerators nationwide, standing as a trusted generational symbol of authentic kitchen trust and reliable domestic comfort.

Yet as contemporary visual culture evolves and supermarket aisles face unprecedented international competition, legacy Egyptian corporate market leaders must periodically revitalize their corporate presence without alienating their loyal customer base. The strategic brief behind this independent redesign concept was to elevate Juhayna's visual stature, infusing its classic packaging and diverse consumer touchpoints with refined modern elegance, organic freshness, and crisp shelf visibility across all major product categories.

By honoring the deep emotional connection Egyptian consumers maintain with the heritage packaging, this concept preserves the indispensable brand markers while systematically resolving typographic tensions, color flatness, and structural stiffness. The result is a revitalized corporate identity that feels simultaneously reassuringly timeless and vibrantly modern, reaffirming Juhayna's unchallenged position as the country's most cherished everyday dairy and fruit juice provider.
direction: Rebranding requires a different skill set from building a brand from scratch. It's not just about improving a mark, it's about correctly identifying what actually needs to change, and just as importantly, what needs to stay exactly as it is.

In Juhayna's case, the flower shape and its gradient are among the most recognizable marks in Egypt. Changing that wasn't an option, and this approach doesn't. Instead, a beam of light was introduced at the center of the flower, and the gradients themselves were reworked to feel more natural, less flat, and more alive, while staying unmistakably Juhayna.

The typography took the same philosophy. The current wordmark is genuinely well made, the smiling يـ and y in both the English and Arabic is a lovely detail, but the letterforms themselves feel a little stiff, and the English and Arabic don't quite read as coming from the same type family. This approach closes that gap: both scripts now share the same closings and angles, and both carry a slight curve throughout, echoing the same smile that's already hidden in the يـ, just carried through the whole wordmark instead of a single letter, and in a more subtle, less literal way.
